traces.answer:
Who said that AI means everything in SaaS needs to be a personalized experience?
Anneka Gupta
AI will also have an impact on how we think about personalization. It used to take weeks to get your first lead back when you launched a new feature, now you can do it in hours and days, which makes it more practical. We’re going to start looking at this differently. But I don’t know if we’ll end up there. That being said, AI is part of it, platforms are part of it. And promises are part of it. The promises around what customers expect for AI capabilities. A lot of these things are aspirational. But they’re good to talk about because they help us set goals for our companies. What should we be doing next year versus what should we be trying out next year? Some of these features aren’t even possible yet. There are some cool use cases where you can tell AI to build a report based on a bunch of data and it builds something pretty nice. But then if you ask it to go and make changes to that report, it fails miserably. So some of these things just aren’t ready yet. They’re interesting to think about though. You asked me three questions. One, will people buy more products per company? Two, will NRR come down as you scale? Three, will driving up ACVs drive acceleration? My answer to number one is yes. In my previous life, I sold a very verticalized solution to retailers. It did very well. But they would never buy another product from anyone else.

traces.answer: So I did want to step back on this because one thing we know is almost everyone in B2B software now wants to use AI to personalize the customer experience more than ever before.
